newsitem.title: USA: Kelley Oil reserves up 50 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Kelley Oil reserves up 50 pct in 1996.

text.p: Kelley Oil & Gas Corp said Thursday its proven reserves increased 50 percent in 1996.
The company also said directors approved a capital expenditure budget for 1997 of about $34 million.

That compares to nearly $52 million spent last year, a spokeswoman said. The 1996 spending included $37.9 million for drilling and recompletions, $2.2 million for lease acquisitions and $11.6 million for acquisitions, she said.
The 1997 funds are primarily for continuing development activities in north Louisiana, Kelley Oil said.
The company said it anticipates 1997 total production to be substantially above the 24.9 billion cubic feet equivalent achieved in 1996, which was up 19 percent from 1995.

Kelley Oil said its increased focus on development activities last year resulted in proved reserves of 306.4 billion cubic feet on an equivalent basis, a net increase of 50 percent, which includes 131.6 billion cubic feet in extensions and discoveries.
The company said its proved developed reserves increased to 179 billion cubic feet equivalent at year-end from 118 billion cubic feet a year earlier.
The company's proved reserves are 97 percent natural gas and essentially all located in Louisiana, it said.

The present value of estimated future net cash flows before income tax, discounted at 10 percent, and using year-end prices, increased to $518 million at year-end 1996, compared to $176 million at year-end 1995.

Kelley Oil said consolidated natural gas, condensate and oil production increased 19 percent last year while production expenses decreased to $0.43 per thousand cubic feet equivalent from $0.55 in 1995.
It said natural gas comprised over 94 percent of the total production in 1996, or 23.5 billion cubic feet.
Production in the fourth quarter of 1996 rose 48 percent 7.6 billion cubic feet equivalent and production expenses per thousand cubic feet dropped 33 percent to $0.41.
During 1996, the company said, it participated in 69 gross development wells in Louisiana, of which 66 were either completed or being completed as of year end for a completion rate of 95 percent.
For the year, Kelley Oil said, it added 100.5 billion cubic feet equivalent of proved reserves through extensions and discoveries. These new additions alone replaced 404 percent of 1996 production.

The company said its purchase of 31.2 billion cubic feet of proved undeveloped reserves in north Louisiana fields operated by the Company replaced an additional 125 percent of 1996 production. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
